title: hided WebSocket contract
description: Handshake, server frames, close reason codes, path refusal reason codes, and client dispatch events for hided.

have_terminal_sequence.description: The `terminal_sequence` of the last terminal frame a reconnecting client applied. With a delta it resumes every pane from there (a pane the hub's ring no longer reaches is drawn again from a full frame); a client that kept its terminals and names none has every pane drawn again; a client given a whole snapshot ignores it.

workspaceQuery.description: A pane-scoped query on a capability-authenticated WebSocket. The daemon derives device, pane, and Workspace from the credential and current core projection.

factoryQuestionGuard.description: One bounded readonly check against an already-open Factory. Only an attested pane on its issuing connection may ask. A successful workspace_result has result.deny true only for the current Task-held spawn joined to its fresh native execution; every unresolved identity or failure allows the hook tool.

linksQuery.description: `hide links`: a read of the link record on a capability-authenticated WebSocket, answered as a workspace_result without a shell. The caller checkout's Project is the scope unless all_projects is set; a target only another Project holds is refused with other_project, and one the record never saw with not_found.

workspaceAction.description: One pane-scoped document or View transition. Repeating the same request ID and command returns its recorded result within the ten-minute retry window.

workspaceResult.description: A pane-scoped request outcome. A successful action result includes context, request_id, changed, view_id, and optionally area_id; a refusal names reason and next_action.

serverFrame.description: snapshot/delta carry the core state; terminal carries pane output beside them, never through the core (see terminalFrame); error answers a malformed client event; directory_list answers a `file_list`, and path_refused answers any event whose path failed its boundary - the $HOME line for `create_workspace` and `clone_repository`, the checkout-root line for `file_list`, `file_open`, `reveal_path`, `file_save`, `file_create`, `dir_create`, `path_rename`, `path_move`, `path_trash` and `file_bytes` (see directoryList and pathRefused). A `file_list`, `file_open`, `reveal_path`, `file_save`, `file_create`, `dir_create`, `path_rename`, `path_move` or `path_trash` that names an SSH device in `device_id` never meets this machine's checkout roots: the core accepts it only for the checkout in front on that device and the device's helper confines every path to that checkout's opened root. file_bytes_error answers a `file_bytes` read the daemon could not serve as bytes (see fileBytes). directory_unavailable answers a `file_list` for a checkout on an SSH device that its helper could not list (see directoryUnavailable). directory_changed announces that a watched folder changed, so the client re-reads that one folder (see directoryChanged). attachment_refused answers an `attachment_stage` or `attachment_commit` that could not be staged (see attachments). file_index_result answers a `file_index` query with the ranked checkout paths (see fileIndex). project_target answers a `project_target` probe (see projectTarget and projectTargetResult). clone_target answers a `clone_target` question about where a clone would land (see cloneTarget). daemon is the first frame after a valid handshake and describes the daemon itself (see daemonInfo). A `file_bytes` read that succeeds is answered with one or more binary frames on the same socket, not a text frame (see fileBytes).

terminalFrame.description: Payload of a terminal frame: pane output from the screen-side hub (PRD core-host-node-terminal D-11, D-22), in the order the panes' nodes produced it. One sequence numbers every pane's chunks; terminal_sequence is the client's cursor after this frame, which it names as have_terminal_sequence when it reconnects. After a whole snapshot the client resets every terminal and is sent a terminal frame with no chunks that gives its new cursor. A pane whose output a client left unsent past 1 MiB, or that a resume cannot reach, sends that client nothing more until a full frame redraws it. Keys go the other way as the `key` event {pane_id or pending_request, bytes_base64}, and a view's grid as `terminal_viewport` {pane_id, cols, rows, new_view}; both reach the pane's node directly and never the core.

daemonInfo.description: Payload of the daemon frame, sent once after a valid handshake and before the first snapshot: what the Settings General tab shows about the daemon. It never carries the token or environment values other than the paths named here; herdr_bin_path and herdr_socket_path are null when the daemon has none. host_id names this daemon host across restarts (`host-` and 32 hex digits, kept in the state directory's `host-id` file); the web shell files unsaved drafts under it, so a draft written against one Hide host is never opened by another that serves the same browser origin. host_name is the name of the machine the daemon runs on, which Settings names as the owner of every value the daemon stores; null when the system does not report one. The daemon also owns the core's one Settings observation flag: a client's `ai_settings` event with `observing` records only that connection's demand, the flag follows the first observer in and the last one out, and a connection that closes releases its demand.

directoryChanged.description: Payload of a directory_changed frame: the watched folder whose contents changed. The daemon watches the focused checkout's root and its most recently expanded folders, at most 64 in total (the root counts); a change within 200 ms of the last one for the same folder is coalesced into the frame already sent. A client re-reads the one folder this names, which is the Explorer's live refresh without a reload. device_id names the device the folder is on: `local` for the daemon's own machine, polled from opened handles every 200 ms, or an SSH device whose helper stamps the selected device's front checkout root and watched folders (the same 64) every 2 s while its Explorer is showing and its helper is ready; a client ignores a frame for a device it is not showing.

providerUsage.description: One row of a snapshot's `navigator.provider_usage`: a provider's seven-day account window as herdr-core/src/usage.rs reads it (docs/AI_PROVIDERS.md, Weekly usage display). state is `loading` until the first read answers, `available` for a current read, `stale` for a success kept while the provider is offline (message says how old), `fallback` for Codex's latest local session window, and `unavailable` with message saying why, a window whose reset has passed included. used_percent and resets_at_unix_seconds are null in `loading` and `unavailable`. buckets are scoped windows under the row, such as one model's own weekly limit.

providerUsageBucket.description: A scoped window under a providerUsage row. state is the row's own `available` or `stale` while the bucket has a value, and `unavailable` with message when its line could not be read or its reset has passed.

uiStateUsageHints.description: Two fields a `ui_state_update` payload may carry beside the UI state it replaces; the core never persists or echoes them, and an absent field keeps the core's value. usage_window_visible: a shell window is on screen, so the core reads each provider every five minutes. usage_popover_open: the Weekly Usage popover is open; its change from false to true reads again any provider last read more than a minute ago.

focusCheckoutPayload.description: focus_checkout: one admitted focus and optional sidebar disclosure transition. Unknown workspace/checkout refuses the disclosure intent before either value changes.

interfaceLanguage.description: The core's shared explicit interface language. Null follows each client's primary system language, with English for unsupported languages. Invalid stored values publish en with a diagnostic and remain stored until an explicit edit.

interfaceLanguageSetPayload.description: Payload of interface_language_set. This event alone edits the core preference; ui_state_update never changes it.

pathRefusalReason.description: outside_home: the real path is not under $HOME (a symlink target counts). home_root: $HOME itself cannot be a workspace. outside_checkout: the path is not under any registered checkout root, which is the reason an explorer event gets for a path under $HOME that no checkout covers. not_found: nothing exists there. not_a_directory: a file where a directory was needed. not_a_file: a directory where a file's bytes were needed. invalid_path: empty, relative, contains `..` or NUL, or an item name that is empty, `.`, `..`, or holds a `/`. already_exists: a `create_workspace` with `new_folder` names a folder where something other than an empty folder (or one holding only `.git` and `.DS_Store`) already stands.

directoryList.description: Payload of a directory_list frame. kind names the event that asked: a `file_list` lists the children of a folder under a registered checkout root - files and directories, hidden names included, `.git` and a symlink that leaves the root absent, directories first and then the natural name order the macOS Explorer uses. root_path is the real path that was listed. is_directory is what the Explorer draws and opens by. truncated is true past the listing cap. device_id names the machine the listing came from: absent for this daemon's own machine, and an SSH device's id for a `file_list` that named that device, whose paths are that device's and are never read here.

inode.description: The entry's own inode (a link's, not its target's) in a `file_list` answer, as decimal text: the identity a `path_trash` of this row sends back unchanged, so the host moves only the item the operator confirmed. Text because a JSON number reaches the browser as a double, which rounds a 64-bit id past 2^53 (an NTFS file id once its sequence number reaches 32).

directoryUnavailable.description: Payload of a directory_unavailable frame: a `file_list` for a checkout on an SSH device that did not come back as a listing. code says what the Explorer offers next: `not_ready` (no helper connection: consent missing or withdrawn, or the device unreachable; nothing was sent), `busy` (the device's request queue is full; nothing was sent), `unknown` (the request was sent and no answer arrived), or `refused` (the helper answered with a refusal such as a replaced root or a missing folder). message is the sentence to show, and root_path is the folder that was asked for.

pathRefused.description: Payload of a path_refused frame: the event kind that carried the path, the path as sent, and why hided did not forward it. A `file_create` or `dir_create` whose name failed the shape check, and a `path_rename` whose new name did, carry that name as the path. A `browser_open`, a `browser_state`, or a `view_layout` navigate whose `url` is a `file:` address is checked like any path: the path it decodes to has to be under a registered checkout root, and the event reaches the core with the `file:` URL of the checked path; a refusal carries the decoded path, or the address as sent when it names another host or does not decode (`invalid_path`).

cloneTarget.description: Add a project's Clone from URL asks where a clone would land with a `clone_target` event {parent, name} while the operator types, and hided answers this frame without forwarding the event: parent and name as sent, path the canonical folder the clone would create when it may, and reason null or the `$HOME` line's refusal, `already_exists` when anything (a folder, even an empty one or a `.git`-only leftover, a file, a dangling symlink) already holds the name. parent may be home itself or `~`; name is one plain folder name. The `clone_repository` event {url, parent, name} passes the same check, reaches the core with parent rewritten to its canonical spelling, or is answered with path_refused naming `parent/name`. The core then refuses a URL it cannot clone or a name the URL does not give, and reports the clone in the snapshot's repository_clone.

openExternal.description: A browser WebSocket client open_external event is always answered with open_external_result {path, ok:false, reason:"untrusted_client"}, even with a valid token and loopback Origin: localhost may be forwarded from another machine. The bare S3 browser downloads oversized files through file_bytes. The bounded host opener remains implemented for a future transport that can establish local ownership (macOS open, Windows ShellExecuteW default association, Linux xdg-open, or validated absolute HIDE_OPEN_COMMAND); no such transport is present in S3. Windows never passes the pathname through cmd.

openExternalResult.description: Payload of an open_external_result frame: the path supplied by the client, ok false, and reason untrusted_client. The browser WebSocket has no authority to launch the daemon host handler. The retained host opener may later report spawn_failed, over_budget, not_found, or not_openable on a separately authenticated local transport.

attachments.description: The web cannot name a dropped file's path, so it uploads bytes for hided to stage, then commits them. `attachment_stage` {request_id, name, size, clipboard} opens one staged file (an over-cap size is refused at once); the bytes follow as binary frames, each framed like a file_bytes frame but client to server: a 4-byte big-endian header length, the header JSON {request_id, offset, eof}, then that chunk's bytes. `attachment_commit` {request_id, pane_id, bracketed_paste, clipboard, stages} turns the staged files into the one `terminal_attachment` event a shell sends for a batch of paths, with the staged paths as its `paths`; a clipboard commit names no paths, because the image was staged at the path the core reads it from, and hided then reports `terminal_attachment_ready` itself. Caps: 20 MiB per file, 40 MiB and 8 files per batch. hided answers `attachment_refused` {request_id, reason} when a stage or commit fails or exceeds a cap; reason is one of invalid_request_id, too_large, batch_too_large, too_many_files, staging_full, size_mismatch, stage_failed, forward_failed, no_pane, unknown_stage, stage_incomplete. Each stage id and name is flattened to one path component and refused otherwise; one id and one path identify one stage, and a second stage may not reuse either. A stage whose bytes do not match its declared size is dropped at eof (size_mismatch). Every arriving byte is charged to a 256 MiB staged budget as it lands (a freshly committed file is spared for 60 s, and a full set of them refuses the new stage rather than unlinking one), hided's own attachments directory starts empty on each run, staged files and their directories are mode 0600/0700, a batch names each stage once and its request id must be the 36-character UUID the core requires, a clipboard stage id must be that shape too because the core derives its path from it, a completed stage leaves the open-upload cap, a connection's uncommitted stages are released when it goes, and a cancel never unlinks a file the core was already told about. A clipboard commit must name exactly the one stage that wrote its image, and that stage must have been opened as a clipboard stage; each mode commits only its own root. The shell's own attachment events (terminal_attachment, terminal_attachment_ready, terminal_attachment_action) are the daemon's to send: a client that sends one is answered with an error frame and it never reaches the core. The core still owns the terminal side: its own refusal arrives in the snapshot's async operations.

attachmentRefused.description: Payload of an attachment_refused frame: the request that failed and why nothing was staged.

projectTarget.description: A client `project_target` event asks where Add a project's Create new project would make a folder: {parent, name}. hided answers it on the $HOME line with a project_target frame and never forwards it; it reads the parent and the one name under it and changes nothing on disk. The create itself is a `create_workspace` with `new_folder: true` and `initialize_git: true` whose `path` is the parent and the name joined by `/`: hided checks the parent on the $HOME line (home itself is allowed, since the new folder is under it) and the name as one folder name, refuses anything already standing at the target except an empty folder or one holding only `.git` and `.DS_Store` (what an earlier attempt that failed after making its folder leaves, so a retry continues into it) as already_exists, and forwards the canonical target; the core makes the folder at that literal path before canonicalizing it, so a symlink planted at the name is refused rather than followed, runs `git init` in it, and registers it. A `new_folder` create that names an SSH device is refused by the core.

projectTargetResult.description: Payload of a project_target frame: the parent and name as sent; the canonical parent and its `~` spelling when the parent resolved; the canonical target when the name was checked too; whether an empty leftover folder is already there and will be used; and the path refusal reason the create would get, or null. An empty name checks the parent alone.

fileIndex.description: A client `file_index` event asks for the files of a registered checkout that match a query: {root, query}. The daemon walks the checkout once, honoring .gitignore (and .git/info/exclude and the global ignore file) without a git process, caps the index at 50,000 files, and answers with a file_index_result frame: {root_path, query, files: [{path, relative_path}], truncated, indexing}. `files` is ranked by the palette's fuzzy score, best first, at most 80; `path` is absolute so the client can open it, `relative_path` is what the palette shows. The first query for a root answers `indexing: true` while the walk runs; `truncated` marks a checkout whose index hit the cap. A root that is not a registered checkout is the usual path_refused frame with kind file_index. With `device_id` naming an SSH device, `root` is a checkout the core's catalog carries for that device, the walk is that device's helper's, `path` is spelled on that device, and a walk the helper could not make is answered with `unavailable` naming why; the next query walks again.

fileIndexResult.description: Payload of a file_index_result frame: the device and root that were searched, the query, the ranked files, whether the index is truncated, whether the walk is still running, and why a device walk was unavailable.

fileBytes.description: A client `file_bytes` event asks for a regular file's bytes under a registered checkout root: {request_id, path, offset, length}. `length` null or absent reads to the end of the file; `offset` defaults to 0. The daemon answers with one or more binary frames, each framed as a 4-byte big-endian header length, the header JSON as UTF-8, then that chunk's bytes. The header is {type: "file_bytes", request_id, path, offset, total, eof}: offset is where this chunk starts in the file, total is the file's whole size, and eof marks the last frame. A read past MAX_FILE_BYTES (256 MiB) or a disk failure is answered with a file_bytes_error text frame instead: {request_id, path, reason} where reason is too_large or read_failed; a device read that a newer one from the same client ended (at most two run per client) is answered with reason superseded. A path that fails the boundary is the usual path_refused frame with kind file_bytes. With `device_id` naming an SSH device and `root` a checkout the core's catalog carries for it, `path` is spelled under that root on the device and the device's helper reads it one bounded range at a time; a file that changes between ranges ends the read as read_failed.

fileBytesError.description: Payload of a file_bytes_error frame: the read that failed and why.
